newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kajiyama says wants full probe into Nomura scandal.
newsitem.headline: Kajiyama says wants full probe into Nomura scandal.

text.p: Japan's chief government spokesman said on Friday that the government wants a full-fledged investigation into the scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd and illegal payoffs to a corporate racketeer.
Speaking to reporters after Tokyo prosecutors arrested former Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki over the scandal, Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama said: "It (The arrest) is extremely regrettable.
"The government wants a no-holds-barred, full-fledged investigation into the scandal to restore public confidence in the entire securities industry," he added.
"We want this arrest to bring about sound management in the securities industry."
Tokyo prosecutors arrested Sakamaki on Friday on suspicion of violating Japan's securities exchange law and the commercial code.
